messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging maya (oncall). Elevated 5xx/error rate observed on streaming gateway (us-west-2) starting ~3890005600. Metric: streaming_gateway.5xx_rate = 4.8% (5m) up from 0.2%. Affected paths: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream. Suspected correlation with recent deploy 3890005500.

maya (oncall): ack. grabbing dashboard and logs. Is this customer-impacting?

chris (support): seeing several customer-reported disconnects on hosted API — two enterprise seats reported mid-request truncation and reconnect loops. Tickets open.

alex (infra): looking at gateway logs — lots of upstream 502 and downstream resets. Stack traces show 'chunked decoder: unexpected EOF' and repeated client cancellations. Could be a fanout amplification to model backends.

sam (runtime): I see a deploy (deploy-bot: deploy 3890005500 -> gateway v3.2.1) at +5m before spike. That change added 'concurrent_stream_fanout' default bump from 8->16. Might be causing backend overload.

maya (oncall): timeline: deploy at 3890005500, spike at ~3890005600, paging at 3890005678. Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) revert fanout setting or lower it 2) enable paged fallback for long-running streams 3) rate-limit new streaming sessions for non-provisioned customers. Which is fastest?

alex (infra): fastest is to roll back config on gateway to previous fanout: patch below. Pushing a config rollback now.

alex (infra): ```
# gateway-config patch
spec.stream.concurrent_fanout: 8  # rollback to previous
kubectl apply -f gateway-config.yaml
```

deploy-bot: rollback triggered: rolling restart gateway deployment (start)

maya (oncall): while rollback kicks in, enable a temporary routing policy to route traffic for enterprise tier -> dedicated-pool to protect SLAs. alex, can you add a route rule?

alex (infra): adding rule now. command: ```
./rctl route add --match 'customer.tier:enterprise && path:/v1/stream' --backend dedicated-pool-usw2 --priority 100
```

alex (infra): rule applied. verifying traffic shift...

lia (sre): quick metric check: 5xx rate dropped from 4.8% -> 1.2% within 30s of route change and rollback beginning. Client cancels still shown but reduced.

chris (support): emailed affected customers with workaround: 'use paged (non-streaming) endpoint or retry' and said we have mitigation ongoing. One customer asked for ETA; told them under investigation and we'll follow up in 1h.

maya (oncall): good. capture traces for one failing request: alex can you paste a sample trace/span?

alex (infra): trace id: trace/0a1b2c3d4e. Excerpt: "upstream write to backend timed out after 15s; gateway attempted chunked-forward, received RST_STREAM from backend, then client Cancelled. backend logs show queue depth spike and async worker OOMs in model shard 7."

sam (runtime): model shard 7 shows memory pressure — OOM kills correlate with increased concurrent_stream_fanout. We'll throttle fanout to 4 for model-heavy routes as a safety cap. Patch: ```
spec.stream.concurrent_fanout: 4
spec.stream.per_model_caps: {"*": 4}
```

alex (infra): applied per-model cap. monitoring.

lia (sre): current metrics: streaming_gateway.5xx_rate = 0.45% (5m), downstream timeouts down to baseline. Latency spiked for a minute but falling.

maya (oncall): good progress. chris, update customers: mitigation applied (rollback + routing + caps), errors significantly reduced, monitoring for 1h.

chris (support): updated clients. one wants a postmortem and timeline. I'll collect affected request IDs and customer traces.

maya (oncall): handoff notes for next oncall (sam): - root cause suspect: aggressive fanout change in gateway deploy 3890005500 causing model shard OOMs and chunked encoding resets. - mitigations applied: rollback fanout to 8, route enterprise traffic to dedicated pool, add per-model cap 4, temporary rate-limit new streaming sessions for non-provisioned. - customer impact: partial truncation/disconnects for some streamed responses; no data loss reported beyond truncated responses; affected customers notified. - evidence: trace/0a1b2c3d4e, deploy 3890005500, metrics time series included in incident doc.

sam (runtime): ack. will keep monitoring through morning and prepare a hotfix to hard-cap fanout and add graceful backpressure (reject with 429 instead of half-complete stream) as next step.

maya (oncall): closing active page — we remain in mitigation mode. If error rate creeps back above 1% for 10m, re-open. thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident status updated -> mitigated. Incident ticket created INC-3890 and assigned to runtime/infra for followup postmortem.
